source.title: Sharpness-aware Orthogonalized Momentum Algorithms
source.authors: Geetika; Shivani Singh Chauhan; Gauranshi Gupta; Anant Jain; K. Kalyanaraman; Bapi Chatterjee

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and supplementary material.
record.tranche_reason: Tests sharpness-aware optimization in synthetic heavy-tailed-noise problems, continued language-model pretraining, CIFAR-10 training, quantization and fine-tuning; it does not test the listed versions' original natural-label generalization settings.
record.gate_note: Results compare optimizer and sharpness-aware variants on validation accuracy, perplexity, loss, quantization sensitivity and forgetting. Cited findings about generalization, sharpness and other optimizers are prior work, not rows. Hyperparameter choices and convergence bounds are not empirical result rows.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares AdamW with momentum SGD on CIFAR-10 and language-model validation performance, bearing on V4 in new settings. These comparisons are missing from the extracted rows. Its sharpness-aware optimization results do not test V7's magnitude-aware sharpness–generalization-gap correlation.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: optimizer family largely determines heavy-tail robustness; spectral geometry helps Muon; SOMA preserves language-model training quality at about 3% additional runtime, moderately improves quantization robustness, and reduces forgetting only slightly. The forgetting setup is internally inconsistent between implementation prose and captions.
record.recipe_differences: Sharpness-aware Muon algorithms and synthetic heavy-tailed-noise experiments, with continued pretraining, quantization and fine-tuning; not the original claim's natural-label/random-label, width, architecture-comparison or generalization-measure recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: Tail index and noise structure change optimizer performance; perturbation radius affects performance, with the best radius generally smaller under lighter tails. Fresh versus stale perturbations, perturbation geometry, model, dataset, training stage and fine-tuning dataset also change outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Under anisotropic heavy-tailed synthetic noise, AdamW-family accuracy is approximately 29%, SGD-family accuracy approximately 36%, and Muon-family accuracy 38–40%; optimizer rankings change with noise structure.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer robustness to simulated heavy-tailed gradient noise depends on its anisotropy.

fits_no_version.finding: Spectral perturbations reduce Muon's optimality gap most under heavy-tailed noise, with much smaller SOMA gains under lighter tails.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral sharpness-aware perturbations can improve optimization under heavy-tailed noise.

fits_no_version.finding: SOMA approximately preserves Muon's validation performance in the reported language-model and CNN runs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Stale spectral perturbations can preserve the base optimizer's held-out performance while avoiding a second gradient evaluation.

fits_no_version.finding: On Pythia-70M, SOMA reduces the INT4 perplexity increase from 10.96% to 10.55%; nanoGPT's quantized perplexity is nearly unchanged across the Muon family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware training can moderately improve post-training quantization robustness, depending on the model.

fits_no_version.finding: Sharpness-aware Muon methods moderately reduce nanoGPT forgetting, especially with fresh perturbations; Pythia-70M shows little difference within the Muon family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Effects of sharpness-aware optimization on forgetting depend on model and perturbation scheme.

record.problems: Synthetic classification and optimization studies use small teacher-student networks and simulated noise; they do not test natural-label random-label memorization or train-test gaps. LLM/CNN experiments are limited to the stated models, datasets and training schedules. Fine-tuning comparisons start from AdamW-pretrained models, and SGD runs are explicitly marked not comparable because their starting loss is weaker.
record.rows_left_out: No required version-specific rows exist because none of V1–V8 is tested. Other reported optimizer outcomes are not catalog rows for these versions. The numeric details of multi-method tables and per-dataset forgetting are not exhaustively extracted because they measure settings outside the mapped versions.

untested.parts: Fixed random-label fitting and held-out performance compared with natural-label training.
Width sweeps beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.

Whether adaptive methods fare worse under tuning restricted to learning rates and schedules on language models; causal effects of broader tuning, decoupling weight decay, or switching from Adam to SGD. Language-model AdamW receives additional weight-decay tuning, and no coupled-decay Adam control is reported.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Dropout additions, dropout strength, small-data regimes, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Measured magnitude-aware sharpness, its correlation with train–test gaps at comparable training loss, and ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removal of highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

missing.what: Add the direct CIFAR-10 AdamW-versus-SGD comparison: validation accuracy 87.87±0.53% versus 84.66±0.40%; training loss 0.316±0.002 versus 0.461±0.003. Both use weight decay 0.0005; SGD uses Nesterov momentum 0.9. These results were incorrectly excluded as unrelated to V4.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's blanket exclusion of V4 is incorrect: direct AdamW-versus-SGD benchmark comparisons bear on it even though the paper primarily develops SOMA. Existing SOMA-versus-Muon rows cannot stand in for those comparisons. No listed original source is this study.

versions.untested_parts: Network-width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified image and language benchmark tuning conditions.
Large versus small batch training under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout effects and removal of dropout with data augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness measurements and their correlation with train-test gaps.
Removing highly memorized training examples and comparing test accuracy.

relationships.condition: Airbench CNN on CIFAR-10, seven epochs, learning-rate search, AdamW versus Nesterov SGD.
relationships.reason: Missing Table 12 comparisons show AdamW accuracy 87.87±0.53% versus SGD 84.66±0.40%, with lower training loss as well; adaptive optimization performs better here. This qualifies the adaptive-worse tendency and is compatible with V4's AdamW exception.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly achieved higher accuracy and lower training loss than Nesterov SGD, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: Continued pretraining of nanoGPT and Pythia-70M on FineWeb-Edu, with additional AdamW weight-decay tuning.
relationships.reason: Missing Table 12 comparisons show AdamW perplexity 24.60±0.02 versus SGD 25.75±0.02 on nanoGPT, and 36.20±0.02 versus 40.03±0.01 on Pythia. Adaptive optimization performs better under this broader tuning recipe; this does not establish what restricted tuning would yield.
relationships.display_finding: AdamW reportedly achieved lower perplexity on both language models with additional weight-decay tuning, but these comparisons remain unverified.
